newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Wife kills Nicaraguan police chief, children, self.
newsitem.headline: Wife kills Nicaraguan police chief, children, self.

text.p: The pregnant wife of the head of Nicaragua's anti-riot police killed him, their two children and herself on Thursday, police said.

Initial police investigations showed that Ernestina Orozco, 30, shot her husband, Subcommander Manuel Lezama, 34, and their two children in the head with a .38-calibre pistol before turning the gun on herself.

Nicaraguan police chief Franco Montealegre told a news conference neighbours reported hearing shots at 7:20 a.m. EDT (1120 GMT) and when police entered the house, they found the four people dead, each with one bullet in the head.
In a note addressed to police, Orozco said she did it because of almost $100,000 in debts she had accumulated buying and selling bonds and because of personal problems with her husband.
The crime shook Nicaragua, which is being hit by rising waves of crime and suicide, Montealegre said.

"It's a sign of the enormous decomposition of our society," congressman and presidential candidate Alfredo Cesar told reporters. "If it could happen to a police commander in his own home, it could happen to any of us."
Lezama headed the special anti-riot squad that was formed to protect Nicaragua's Oct. 20 general elections.
Police said they had found no link between his job and the murder. They have not announced his replacement.
